children: Shares of Canadian copper producers were in retreat on Wednesday as prices for the industrial metal sank to their lowest level since April amid a selloff in AI-related stocks and worries about demand in China.

Teck Mining, which tightened its focus on copper after selling its coal assets, was down 6% at C$75.27 to narrow the year-to-date advance to 15%. Diversified miner Lundin Mining, which aims to become a global 10 top copper producer, was down 10% at C$24.64, for a drop of 17% so far this year.

Three-month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange declined more than 5% in midmorning North American trading, to below $13,0000 per metric ton as the U.S. dollar strengthened and investors turned away from bets tied to the boom in artificial intelligence. The selling also reflected investor worries about demand, traditional industrial activity and the health of China's economy.
Among other Toronto-listed names, First Quantum slid 10% to C$24.62, Hudbay Minerals was off by  9.1% at C$25.61, Capstone Copper declined 6.7% to C$8.64, and Ero Copper sank 12% to C$33.95.
